text: 🇲🇽✊ "I propose we stop calling this territory 'Paso de Cortés' — the peoples passed through here long before. Today, on the International Day of Indigenous Peoples, let us call it 'El Paso de los Pueblos Indígenas'." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Izta-Popo pass, Puebla The pass between the Popocatépetl and Iztaccíhuatl volcanoes has been called "Paso de Cortés" since 1519, when Cortés crossed it toward Tenochtitlán after the Cholula massacre. Sheinbaum announced the renaming at the launch of National Reforestation Day in Santiago Xalitzintla.

🇲🇽🌳 1.2 billion trees planted in eight years — today, 6.6 million more in a single day. Sembrando Vida has planted 1.2 billion timber and fruit trees and reforested over 1 million hectares in eight years. The stakes, per Environment Secretary Alicia Bárcena: Mexico holds 12% of the world's biodiversity, and 60% of its forest ecosystems are in ejido and community hands. Deforestation, illegal logging, fires and pests hit over 1.1 million hectares a year — illegal logging is now fought in coordination with the Security Secretariat. — Jornada Nacional de Reforestación, Izta-Popo National Park, Puebla, August 9, 2026

🇲🇽🌳 "From now on, one day a year when each and every one of us plants trees." "El objetivo es que esta jornada sea todos los años, que no solamente sea en 2026, sino que a partir de ahora pongamos un día al año donde todas y todos reforestemos." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo Mexico held its first annual National Reforestation Day today. Sheinbaum led the kickoff at Izta-Popo National Park, Puebla, alongside Governor Alejandro Armenta — with simultaneous plantings in all 32 states: 6.6 million trees and plants across 621 municipalities, with 235,097 participants.
banner: "A DAY WHEN ALL OF US PLANT TREES"

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>HACIENDA TRIMS FUEL TAX STIMULUS: MAGNA IEPS AT 5.30 PESOS/LITER THIS WEEK</u>

El Economista reports: for the week of August 8-14, Mexico's Finance Ministry (SHCP) trimmed the IEPS fiscal stimulus on fuels. Magna's stimulus drops to 20.94% — 1.40 pesos per liter, down from 2.45 — leaving an IEPS quota of 5.30 pesos per liter; Premium's support nearly vanishes (5.77%), while diesel keeps the largest shield at 64.96%: the state absorbs 4.78 pesos of the tax and freight transport pays just 2.58.

The mechanism adjusts every Friday in the DOF, tracking international oil prices — WTI has swung as high as $82.24 a barrel during the Middle East conflict. And diesel, the fuel that moves Mexico's food and freight, is the one that keeps the strongest cushion.
banner: FUEL TAX SHIELD CUT: DIESEL AT 65%

After a 12-hour hearing, federal judge Juan Alfredo Buendía lifted every precautionary measure against Brenda Quevedo Cruz: no more house arrest, no ankle monitor, no National Guard custody. The "Wallace case" was one of the old regime's most notorious frame-ups. Every self-incriminating statement from her co-defendants was extracted under torture, as expert evidence proved. Brenda never signed any confession. No other evidence ever held up.

Why is the case still alive a year and a half after Isabel Miranda de Wallace's death? Almost all of them are still active."

🇲🇽🎓 <u>PRIVATE UNIVERSITIES +200% IN TWO DECADES: THE NEOLIBERAL LEGACY IN HIGHER ED</u>

New data from UNAM researcher Axel Meléndez: enrollment at Mexico's private universities has grown almost 200% in two decades. In Mexico City alone, from 144,493 students in 2000 to 424,878 in 2024 — a constant climb since 2008.

Meanwhile, demand for public education keeps outrunning supply: UNAM applicants grew 62% in a decade (from 179,350 to 290,759), while seats grew just 57% — and many of the new ones are online-only.

"Yes, there were 10,000 more places, no denying it. But what we are discussing is that supply has not grown in line with demand, which increased by more than 100,000 people."
